prompt.context: Our client is one of the top three beverage manufacturers in the US. They are thinking of launching a new non-sparkling flavored water product. The company is a vertically integrated beverage manufacturer that makes the drinks, has five bottling plants, and owns their own distribution channels.
prompt.question: They have asked us to determine whether or not they should launch the new product, how to do it, and what the marketing strategy should be.

clarifying_info.q: What is the size of the entire water market?
What is the breakdown of the water market between sparkling and non-sparkling?
clarifying_info.a: 90% sparkling, 10% non-sparkling. Within the non-sparkling segment, there are two major flavored water competitors: O2 with ~12% share and Easy Drink with ~18% share, with the remainder fragmented among others.

clarifying_info.q: How will the drinks be packaged?
clarifying_info.a: Everyone packages their water in 16oz bottles, and our client will do the same.

clarifying_info.q: How will the drink be priced?
What are the costs per bottle?

exhibits.title: Water Market Breakdown: Sparkling vs. Non-Sparkling
exhibits.shows: A pie or bar chart showing the split of the 8-million-gallon water market between sparkling (90%) and non-sparkling (10%).

exhibits.title: Non-Sparkling Flavored Water Segment Share
exhibits.shows: A breakdown of the 10% non-sparkling portion showing market share by competitor brand.

exhibits.title: Competitor Positioning: How consumers perceive O2 and Easy Drink
exhibits.shows: A chart showing the percentage of survey respondents who categorize O2, Easy Drink, and Other competitors as a low-calorie healthy drink, a sports drink, or a leisure beverage.

framework: Market assessment: size the overall water market and the target non-sparkling flavored water sub-segment
Competitive landscape: identify key players and their market shares
Financial analysis: price/cost/margin per unit, launch investment, break-even volume and timeline
Market positioning: determine how to differentiate from O2 and Easy Drink
Risks and other considerations: cannibalization, market trends, brand extension

questions.prompt: Calculate the size of the flavored non-sparkling water market in bottles per year.
questions.guidance: Candidate should take 10% of the total 8 million gallons, then convert gallons to 16oz bottles using the fact that 1 gallon = 64oz so 4 bottles per gallon.

math.setup: Total water market = 8 million gallons. Non-sparkling share = 10%. Bottles per gallon = 64oz/16oz = 4.
steps: Total non-sparkling bottles = 800,000 x 4 = 3,200,000 bottles per year

questions.prompt: Calculate the margin per bottle and the break-even number of bottles.
questions.guidance: Candidate should identify the 10-cent margin and divide the $400,000 launch cost by that margin. They should then recognize that 4 million bottles exceeds the entire annual market.

math.setup: Price = $1.00 per bottle. Cost = $0.90 per bottle. Launch investment = $400,000.
math.answer: 4 million bottles must be sold to break even — more than the entire annual market of 3.2 million bottles

questions.prompt: Estimate how many years it will take to break even, given a reasonable market share assumption.
questions.guidance: Candidate should reference Exhibit 2 (O2 ~12%, Easy Drink ~18%) and justify a market share target. Using ~15% is reasonable. They should then divide break-even volume by annual bottles captured and note that 8 years is a very long time in the beverage industry.

math.setup: Market share assumption: ~15% of 3.2 million bottles per year. Break-even volume: 4 million bottles.
steps: Annual bottles at 15% share = 15% x 3,200,000 = 480,000 ≈ 0.5 million bottles
math.answer: Approximately 8 years — a very long horizon for a beverage product given how quickly trends change

brainstorming.prompt: What are potential problems or risks with this new venture?

categories.name: Market / Demand Risk
ideas: Flavored water may be a short-lived trend or fad
Consumer preferences in beverages shift rapidly
Category growth may stagnate before break-even is reached

categories.name: Competitive Risk
ideas: Established players (O2, Easy Drink) may respond aggressively on price or promotion
New entrants could further fragment the market

categories.name: Internal / Cannibalization Risk
ideas: New product may cannibalize existing beverages in the client's portfolio
Resources (bottling plant capacity, distribution) may be stretched

categories.name: Financial / Execution Risk
ideas: 8-year break-even is very long for a consumer beverage
Marketing spend may need to be higher to establish brand recognition in an unfamiliar sub-segment

recommendation: This is a questionable investment in its current form: the 8-year break-even horizon is very long for a consumer beverage market where trends shift frequently.

However, if interest in flavored water remains strong and the client can leverage its brand strength and existing distribution to secure market share at the higher end of the range (closer to 20%), the timeline shortens materially and the product has profit potential.

Recommend conditional launch: proceed only if the company can negotiate lower launch costs, achieve a market share above 15% quickly, and confirm that consumer demand for flavored non-sparkling water is durable rather than a passing trend.
risks: Market trend reversal — flavored water loses popularity before break-even
Competitor retaliation compressing margins or market share
next_steps: Conduct consumer research to validate durability of demand and preferred positioning (sports vs. leisure)
Analyze cannibalization impact on existing portfolio
Model sensitivity of break-even timeline to varying market share and launch cost assumptions
Explore whether launch costs can be reduced by leveraging existing bottling and distribution assets more aggressively
